children: Chicago Mercantile Exchange live and feeder cattle futures rallied on Wednesday, while lean hog futures plummeted.
ended the day 0.95 cent higher at 231.125 cents per pound.
finished the day up 2.940 cents at 348.82 cents per pound.
On the Chicago Board of Trade, futures for corn, a feed ingredient dropped, making the feeding of cattle cheaper.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) settled 1-1/4 cents higher at $4.63-1/4 a bushel after falling to three-month lows earlier in the session.

Wholesale boxed beef prices fell at midday on Wednesday to $372.59 per hundredweight (cwt) for choice cuts, down $0.71 from a day earlier, the US Department of Agriculture said. Select cuts fell $6.20 to $355.34 per cwt.

Beef packer margins widened. The average margin on Wednesday was estimated at $50.15 per head, up from $34.50 on Tuesday, but down from $85.00 a week ago, according to livestock marketing advisory service HedgersEdge.
CME lean hog futures dropped to new contract lows after stabilizing on Tuesday, as sluggish demand and weak pork prices created ongoing pressure for the hog market.
The USDA reported wholesale hog carcasses were priced at $74.50 per cwt on Wednesday afternoon, down $4.03 from the previous day.
Pork bellies were reported at $77.66 per cwt, down $12.01 from Tuesday.
December lean hogs (LHZ26) ended 1.425 cent lower at 65.725 cents per pound, after hitting a contract low of 65.700 earlier in the session.
